ns2:section.sectionText: Computational Methods for Systems Engineering This course introduces computational methods for the design and analysis of complex aerospace systems and system-of-systems. We specifically focus on techniques to support operational analysis and conceptual design of such systems, by introducing data-drive methods to model system operations and optimization methods for system design. Topics include linear regression, classification, neural networks, Design of Experiments, surrogate modeling, and multi-objective optimization. Pre-requisites: IE 300 or equivalent statistical analysis course (or permission of the instructor) Graduate Students: 4 hours Restricted to online non-degree, online MCS, online MSME, online MSCEE, and online MSAE students.For more details on this course section, please see http://engineering.illinois.edu/online/courses/. Non-Degree students may enroll on a space-available basis with consent of Program Coordinator, Staci McDannel (tank@illinois.edu).
